name: A/B Testing
description:
A/B testing compares two versions of a design to investigate whether a specific change affects user behaviour or another predefined measure. Participants encounter one of the alternatives and their responses are compared across the two conditions. The method is particularly useful when a design question can be expressed as a clear hypothesis and evaluated using observable measures.

A/B testing can help designers choose between alternatives, but it explains **which version performed differently**, not *why*. Qualitative research may therefore be useful alongside an A/B test.
whenToUse: Use A/B testing when you have two clearly defined alternatives and enough participants or interactions to make a meaningful comparison. It is particularly useful for evaluating focused changes to an existing interface, service, or communication rahter than exploring an undefined design problem.
steps: Identify the design decision you want to investigate.
Form a hypothesis describing the expected effect of the change.
Define a measurable outcome before running the test.
Create two versions that differ primarily in the feature being investigated.
Assign comparable participants or users to each version.
Collect the same measures for both versions.
Compare the results and consider whether the observed difference is meaningful.
Use the findings to inform the next design iteration or further investigation.
lookOutFor: Avoid changing many things simultaneously, as this makes it difficult to determine what caused a difference.
Do not interpret a small numerical difference as evidence without considering sample size, variability, and uncertainty.

Optimising a measurable behaviour does not necessarily mean that the design has become better overall. Consider accessibility, user experience, ethics, and longer-term consequences alongside the selected metric.

resources.citation: Kohavi, R., Tang, D. & Xu, Y. (2020). *Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing*. Cambridge University Press.
